sources.note: Nothing on stress; ethnography. Preface p. xxvii: 'There is no Agaria language, and since these tribesmen live outside the Gondi area they usually speak a corrupt Hindi. The Asur of Neterhat, however, have their own Munda tongue, a so-called Aghori language noted by Sir G. A. Grierson.' P. 53 relays Grierson (LSI IV) on 'a language called Agoria or Agaria' returned from Ranchi and Palamau (1,616 speakers, 'rapidly dying out'), i.e. the Asuri sub-group.
